must_remember: Newton's Law of Cooling is a special linear approximation of the Stefan-Boltzmann law valid only for small temperature differences between the body and its surroundings.
The average temperature method $\frac{T_1 - T_2}{t} = k\left(\frac{T_1 + T_2}{2} - T_0\right)$ is extensively used in UP TGT/PGT examinations to bypass complex exponential integration.
The time constant $\tau = 1/k$ signifies the time required for the excess temperature of a cooling body to reduce to $1/e$ of its initial value.
Equal drops in temperature take increasingly longer time intervals because the cooling rate decreases monotonically as the body approaches ambient temperature.

glossary.meaning: Constant temperature of the surrounding medium or ambient temperature.
Cooling constant dependent on surface area, mass, specific heat, emissivity, and ambient temperature ($s^{-1}$).
Time constant of the cooling process, defined as $\tau = 1/k$.
Mean or average temperature of the body during a given time interval, $(T_1 + T_2)/2$.
